In order to save energy the default interval is 45 seconds. Behind NAT routers that remove mappings early this might be too high, try 20 seconds or less in that case. Send certificate requests Certificate requests are sent for all available or selected CA certificates. To reduce the size of the IKE_AUTH message this can be disabled. However, this only works if the server sends its certificate even if it didn\'t receive any certificate requests. Use OCSP to check certificate Use the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP), if available, to check that the server certificate has not been revoked. Use CRLs to check certificate Use Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL), if available, to check that the server certificate has not been revoked. CRLs are only used if OCSP doesn\'t yield a result. Use strict revocation checking In strict mode the authentication will fail not only if the server certificate has been revoked but also if its status is unknown (e.g. because OCSP failed and no valid CRL was available). Use RSA/PSS signatures Use the stronger PSS encoding instead of the classic PKCS#1 encoding for RSA signatures. Authentication will fail if the server does not support such signatures. Use IPv6 transport addresses Use IPv6 for outer transport addresses if available. Can only be enabled if UDP encapsulation for IPv6 is supported by the server. Note that the Linux kernel only supports this since version 5.8, so many servers will not support it yet. Split tunneling By default, the client will route all network traffic through the VPN, unless the server narrows the subnets when the connection is established, in which case only traffic the server allows will be routed via VPN (by default, all other traffic is routed as if there was no VPN). Block IPv4 traffic not destined for the VPN Block IPv6 traffic not destined for the VPN Custom subnets Only route traffic to specific subnets via VPN, everything else is routed as if there was no VPN (separated by spaces, e.g. \"192.168.1.0/24 2001:db8::/64\") Excluded subnets Traffic to these subnets will not be routed via VPN, but as if there was no VPN (separated by spaces, e.g. \"192.168.1.0/24 2001:db8::/64\") Applications Select applications No applications selected One application selected %1$d applications selected Algorithms Optionally configure specific algorithms to use for IKEv2 and/or IPsec/ESP instead of the defaults. Refer to our wiki for a list of algorithm identifiers (note that not all are supported by this app). Both fields take a list of algorithms, each separated by a hyphen. IKEv2 Algorithms For non-AEAD/classic encryption algorithms, an integrity algorithm, a pseudo random function (optional, defaults to one based on the integrity algorithm) and a Diffie-Hellman group are required (e.g. aes256-sha256-ecp256). For combined-mode/AEAD algorithms, the integrity algorithm is omitted but a PRF is required (e.g. aes256gcm16-prfsha256-ecp256). IPsec/ESP Algorithms For non-AEAD/classic encryption algorithms, an integrity algorithm is required, a Diffie-Hellman group is optional (e.g. aes256-sha256 or aes256-sha256-ecp256). For combined-mode/AEAD algorithms, the integrity algorithm is omitted (e.g. aes256gcm16 or aes256gcm16-ecp256). If a DH group is specified IPsec SA rekeying will use a DH key exchange. However, DH groups specified here are not used when the connection is established initially because the keys there are derived from the IKE SA key material. Therefore, any configuration mismatch with the server will only cause errors later during rekeying. Try another protocol IKEv2 — is the fastest protocol in terms of response time and VPN connection setup. Upon signal loss or network change, it automatically restores connection in a fraction of a second. The protocol is battery-efficient and provides consistently high internet speed using proven data protection technologies.\n\nUnlike alternatives, IKEv2 has a very distinct digital signature. Many providers (and TSPU) easily recognize it by standard ports and its specific key exchange method, so in modern conditions, IKEv2 is often blocked by Russian filtering systems almost instantly. VLESS Reality — is currently one of the most powerful combinations for bypassing blocks. Simply put, it\'s a way to make your VPN traffic absolutely indistinguishable from visiting a regular popular website. It works as fast as possible due to the absence of unnecessary checks, making your traffic look like a regular website.\n\nThe provider sees no signs of a VPN and considers your connection legitimate. When checked by a censor, your server simply pretends to be a known third-party resource. Blocking such a connection is practically impossible without shutting down the entire global internet. This is the most stable and high-speed method of bypassing restrictions today in countries with severe censorship. AmneziaWG — is an evolution of the famous WireGuard, created specifically to work under severe censorship. It has retained the legendary lightness and colossal speed of the original protocol, but has become practically invulnerable to tracking systems. Developers removed the network signatures by which provider DPI systems instantly recognize regular WireGuard.\n\nOur VPN uses the most current version of the protocol, AmneziaWG 2.0. Version 1.5 introduced masking as DNS and QUIC requests, version 2.0 turned the protocol into a true master of mimicry to bypass heuristic analysis. Now, packet headers and sizes constantly change, confusing filtering systems right during data transfer. For TSPU, such a stream looks like ordinary chaotic noise or the standard operation of services. GW — is an independent network protocol built from scratch by our team. We deliberately rejected ready-made templates and add-ons layered on top of third-party technologies. The GW architecture was originally designed to solve complex practical tasks in real-world network conditions. GW delivers minimal connection setup latency, effectively holds the channel when network quality degrades, and remains resilient to harsh external restrictions.\n\nWe keep the protocol\'s architectural details closed. Our goal is to spare users from technical complexities and deliver a flawless result — a stable and fast connection in one click.\n\nThe GW protocol is constantly evolving: we test, refine and optimize it until we achieve exactly the result we aim for.
